title: Normalized reduction and scalar total-limit identification
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$ and $e\geq1$ with $tB=v^eB$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete bounded constructible category with a uniform Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $A_n=A/t^n$, $B_n=B/t^nB=B/v^{en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$. For $H=E,F$, let $P_H^c$ be the integral compact-support functor attached to $c$, defined as the total derived inverse limit of its finite separately derived proper/open images [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

Use the strict reduction lifts $\mathcal T_E^c(M)$ and $\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM)$ of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], restricted to the discrete constant ring sheaves $\underline A$ and $\underline B$. A strict tower means a complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_W))$ or its $B$ analogue, with its ordinary derived category [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A superscript $(e)$ retains indices $en$ with composite transitions. Put $T=-\otimes_A B$ on constant-coefficient tower complexes; all finite coefficient objects are regarded as constant integral modules by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

Use the strict map $q_\bullet^c:T\mathcal T_E^c(M)\to(\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM))^{(e)}$ characterized in [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate]. Let $U_E=\mathcal T_E^c(M)$ and $U_F=\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM)$. Both full towers are normalized DVR towers [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]: for $m\geq n\geq1$ their transition adjuncts $U_{H,m}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^m}\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n\to U_{H,n}$ are the canonical compact-support coefficient isomorphisms and obey the quotient cocycle, for $H=E,F$ separately. Here the $F$-tower is normalized at all powers of $v$, not just powers of $t$.

All total-limit objects in the following display are regarded as derived-complete completed-coefficient objects through the canonical constant/completed equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. For a strict tower $K$ use the Roos model $\mathsf R(K)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod K_n\to\prod K_n)[-1]$, where $(sx)_n$ is the transition applied to $x_{n+1}$ [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality]. The canonical finite-free tensor/product map and the inverse of the canonical cofinal restriction $r_e:\mathsf R(U_F)\to\mathsf R(U_F^{(e)})$ give an isomorphism
$$\gamma_M:C_Y\mathsf R(U_E)\longrightarrow\mathsf R(U_F),\qquad
\gamma_M=r_e^{-1}\,\mathsf R(q_\bullet^c)\,\tau,$$
where $\tau$ is the tensor/product map transported by the constant/completed equivalence and the ordinary/strict scalar comparison $\chi$. This is an isomorphism of the specified derived-limit objects, natural in $M$, preserving the augmentations and the $S_Y$-action.

Under normalized-tower effectivity and the scalar-extension/restriction adjunction, reduction of $\gamma_M$ modulo $t^nS_Y=v^{en}S_Y$ is exactly $q_{n,M}$, and these equalities commute with all further quotient reductions. They hold for the adjoints of the canonical limit projections. For any commuting square of coefficient quotient maps, the corresponding comparison equations are the pasted scalar-mate equations with their common tensor associator; in particular the squares for $A_m\to A_n$ and $B_m\to B_n$ commute for every $m\geq n$.

proof.text: The fixed scalarRoosComparison is unit-normalized. Apply scalarRoosNormalization_of_unit to obtain the selected cofinality map, its quasi-isomorphism and coordinate identities, its derived restriction identification and all strict augmentation equations. The substantial proof is in its own module; the existing scalarRoosNormalization signature and chosen comparison remain unchanged.
For scalarLimitMapAugmentation use roosF_map_χ and roosAugment_χ, biproduct/product extensionality and naturality of the fixed Roos comparison. This sends (0,a) to (0,a composed with q).

Use the integral basis, its constant-sheaf realization and natural finite-power coordinates to prove scalar tensor preserves the required products. Identify the chosen tensor map with the canonical roosAdditiveComparison. The separately compiled, proved scalarRoosTensorNormalization_of_units then gives the actual tensor/limit identity and augmentation equation. Naturality combines all three factors to prove scalarLimitArrow_augmentation.

For the main theorem, compactSupportCoefficientModels_scalar preserves the intrinsic finite-Tor constructible domain. Apply compactSupport_native_realization and compactSupport_native_effectivity separately to M over E and to its scalar extension over F. These yield literal equality of the specified towers, full native normalization, intrinsic completeness, all native quotient cocycles and every specified finite counit isomorphism.

Apply scalarLimitCompletedComparison for the natural completed comparison and its transport and projection equations. Independently obtain invertibility of the actual strict arrow by evaluating compactSupportStrictScalarMate on the finite-Tor subcategory. Each of the three factors in scalarLimitArrow is then invertible.

Transpose the completed projection equation under the F finite scalar adjunction. Naturality on the source map and target balancing map identifies its transpose with extension of gamma followed by scalarSupportPositiveCounit and balancing. Injectivity of homEquiv gives the displayed finite reduction equation. This is implemented by the fully proved abstract projection_adjoint helper.

The final two clauses specialize the already proved comparison_quotients and generic comparisonSquare helpers in IntegralCompactSupportCoefficientComparison. They use only the earlier generic coefficient mate/composition calculus, not that module's later integral comparison theorem. Assemble the fourteen geometric clauses with the same gamma. No parent integral-comparison theorem is used as a dependency.

Stage 3 K2, 2026-10-26: completed the universal uniqueness argument for scalarRoosComparison_existsUnique in Step 3 without changing its statement or adding theorem holes; six existing named theorem holes remain. Stage 3 F5, 2026-10-27: proved scalarCompletion_existsUnique by specializing the completely proved ordinary-balancing localization helper. Five original holes remain; no holes are added. Stage 3 B2, 2026-10-27: proved scalarRoosNormalization, including its derived-unit normalization and strict augmentation identity, by the existing cofinality construction and the canonical cochain formula for rightDerivedPullback. Two theorem holes remain in this item; no new holes or assumptions are introduced. The fully proved abstract calculation is recorded by lem-pur-roos-arithmetic-normalization. To give the parent runtime margin, its already proved comparison-uniqueness theorem is moved verbatim to lem-pur-scalar-roos-comparison-unique; the parent publicly imports its provider, preserving the visible declaration. Stage 3 B3, 2026-10-27: proved scalarRoosTensorNormalization from the strict coordinate comparison, its augmentation formula, and a fully proved abstract comparison with the canonical derived units. One original theorem hole remains; no new holes are added. Stage 3 D4, 2026-10-27: prove the main theorem from the two completely proved native realization/effectivity modules and one strictly smaller completed-comparison statement. Derive finite reduction by adjunction, strict-limit invertibility from the strict mate, and coefficient squares by their existing generic proved helpers. One lower comparison hole is split off; no normalization or effectivity hole remains.

The statement is unchanged, there are no new nodes, stmt_deps and uses match the bracketed citations, proof_deps equals the union of uses, every id exists and no SGA is cited. I read every cited statement. Step 1: normalized-realization (field E for M, field F at all v-levels for C_XM; Tor bounds from coefficient-models) plus the tower functor's transitions, which use the same lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars comparison as the compact-support definition, give normalized DVR towers whose coherent datum is the specified lift. Step 3: det-pe-products-exact gives the exact-products hypothesis of the strict Roos comparison, and coefficient-models gives χ. Step 4: τ and r_e from roos-cofinality and q invertible from strict-scalar-mate give γ=r_e^{-1}R(q)τ with matching types. Step 6: the transpose ε^F_{en}(γ⊗B_n)=q_n C^{(n)}(ε^E_n)d_n follows by adjunction naturality and the associator. Step 7: the ε cocycle, q's quotient squares before the limit and mate-pasting clauses (1)-(2) make it formal. Every argument of the old Q13 Steps 5-6 is retained and made more explicit. Small cases checked: E=F and e=1 (r_1=id, identity mate), M=0, X=∅, e=2 odd levels, n=m. Sources checked: Stacks 0941 (sites-cohomology.tex:5067), 0GL6 (more-etale.tex:3739) and 07A6 (sites-cohomology.tex:3990). There is no duplicate: Q13's sibling nodes cite γ for its projection, composition and shift properties, outside the item's proof_deps, so there is no cycle. The 7 generic tool_uses are accepted.
